from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Fourier Series: Decomposing the Wave", [
            "Fourier series acts as a musical chord.", 
            "Complex signals contain many pure frequencies.", 
            "We sum sine waves of varying amplitudes."
        ])
        
        # Define colors
        color_cyan = "#00FFFF"
        color_yellow = "#FFFF00"
        color_magenta = "#FF00FF"
        color_green = "#00FF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a complex periodic wave; label 'Signal' in #00FFFF.
        signal_axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        signal = signal_axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x) + 0.5 * np.sin(3*x), color=color_cyan)
        label = Text("Signal", color=color_cyan, font_size=24)
        
        self.place_in_area(signal_axes, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(signal, "B3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "A3")
        
        self.play(Create(signal_axes), Create(signal), Write(label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_cyan)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Overlay three sine waves with varying frequencies.
        wave1 = signal_axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x), color=color_yellow)
        wave2 = signal_axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3*x), color=color_magenta)
        wave3 = signal_axes.plot(lambda x: 0.25 * np.sin(5*x), color=color_green)
        
        self.play(Create(wave1), Create(wave2), Create(wave3))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_yellow)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate the sum converging to the original signal.
        sum_wave = VGroup(wave1, wave2, wave3)
        self.play(sum_wave.animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_green)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Connecting to the Heat Equation", [
            "The heat equation describes energy dispersal.",
            "Sine waves remain stable as they decay.",
            "Fourier components solve heat distribution problems."
        ])
        
        # Visuals
        heat_map = Square(side_length=3, fill_opacity=0.6, color=BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(heat_map, "B2", "E5")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color('#FFD700'))
        self.play(FadeIn(heat_map))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color('#00FF00'))
        # Simulate decay smoothing
        self.play(heat_map.animate.set_color(interpolate_color(BLUE, RED, 0.5)))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color('#FF6347'))
        laplacian = MathTex(r"\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = k \nabla^2 u", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(laplacian, "A3")
        self.play(Write(laplacian))
        self.play(laplacian.animate.set_color('#FFFF00'))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visual Synthesis and Application", [
            "Decompose a jagged temperature spike into waves.",
            "Each individual wave component decays over time.",
            "Summing these waves reconstructs smooth heat curves."
        ])
        
        # Colors for lines
        colors = [YELLOW, BLUE, GREEN]
        
        # Setup Axes for the heat plot
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 2, 0.5], x_length=4, y_length=3).shift(DOWN*0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(axes)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(colors[0])
        
        # Show initial jagged spike (approx)
        spike = axes.plot(lambda x: 1.5 if 1.5 < x < 2.5 else 0.5, x_range=[0, 4])
        spike.set_color(colors[0])
        self.play(Create(spike))
        
        # Decompose into waves (simplified)
        waves = VGroup(*[axes.plot(lambda x, n=i: 0.5 * np.sin(n * PI * x), x_range=[0, 4]) for i in range(1, 4)])
        waves.set_color(colors[0])
        self.play(Transform(spike, waves))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(colors[1])
        
        # Waves decay
        self.play(*[wave.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.3) for wave in waves])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(colors[2])
        
        # Summing to smooth curve
        final_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 1.0 + 0.3 * np.sin(2 * PI * x), x_range=[0, 4])
        final_curve.set_color(colors[2])
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(waves, final_curve))
        
        # Pulse highlight
        self.play(final_curve.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(final_curve.animate.scale(1/1.1), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: From Circles to Heat: The Magic of Fourier Series

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Circular Motion Foundation
sections.content: Introduce Euler's formula (e^ix = cosx + isinx) as the building block. Explain that any periodic function can be viewed as the projection of multiple rotating vectors (epicycles) working in harmony.
sections.example: Visualize a robotic arm drawing a complex shape by combining several simple, constant-speed circular rotations.

sections.title: Fourier Series: Decomposing the Wave
sections.content: Define the Fourier series as a 'musical chord' of sine and cosine waves. Explain that any complex periodic signal is just a summation of simple harmonic waves with different frequencies and amplitudes.
sections.example: Think of a synthesizer: a single complex 'piano' note is actually a collection of pure sine wave frequencies playing together.

sections.title: Connecting to the Heat Equation
sections.content: Introduce the 1D heat equation (du/dt = k * d^2u/dx^2). Explain why sine waves are the 'eigenfunctions' of this equation—they keep their shape as they decay, allowing us to solve heat distribution problems by decomposing the initial state into Fourier components.
sections.example: A metal rod heated in the middle: the heat spreads out like a wave smoothing itself out, calculated by tracking how each Fourier frequency component fades over time.

sections.title: Visual Synthesis and Application
sections.content: Show the animation of heat dissipation: An initial jagged temperature spike is decomposed into a set of waves; each wave shrinks exponentially; the sum of these shrunken waves reconstructs the smooth temperature curve over time.
sections.example: A 'Robot Chef' monitoring the temperature of a pizza slice, using Fourier analysis to predict exactly when the cold spots in the dough will reach the perfect baking temperature.
